header.name: Introduction to Digital Ethnography
header.description: This course is intended to be an introductory course and will systematically introduce learners to the basics of digital ethnography. By exposing learners to the fundamentals of Ethnography as a research method, it will help facilitate its application to the online virtual space. The course will use a combination of lectures and case studies to showcase how Digital Ethnography was used to discover significant nuggets of information that was then used to uncover larger trends.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: The course will help learners discern that data are not neutral units of information. It will help reflect on absence of data and also appreciate the importance of small but thick data and will hence complement the big data analytics approach, thus enabling the learner to scale between choosing different research techniques in the long term.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Through an introduction to ethnographic case studies, the learner will be encouraged to apply and incorporate ideas of correlating significant but seemingly tiny clues to a larger canvas.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: The learner would be able to apply basic Digital ethnographic research in a systematic format.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: The learner will be able to present team work to an audience in a creative and easily accessible format.

lecture_topics: Why Ethnography for a Digital World?
Research Design - Strategies for discerning the Everyday Digital
Other Data Collection Methods for Digital Ethnographic Research
Ethnographic Exploration in Digitally Mediated Environment
Ethnographic Obervation in Digitally Mediated Environment

assessments.type_label: Team-based mini-ethnography based on a minimum 6 hours of observation/ participant observation of an online space.
